SECTION 
 
5.11 
PAGE 
 
1 
 
 
SSI PRI-MAX 
TM 
 Service Manual - 991831 Rev 0 
 
 
 
Always lock out and tag out all power to panels and electric components before 
servicing. 
 
 
 
 
On diesel powered systems, disconnect the battery cables to prevent damage to 
the waste reducer electrical system. 
 
 
 
 
Be sure to ground to the object you are welding on.   If you are working on a cutter, 
ground to that cutter or elsewhere on the same cutter shaft.  If you are welding on 
the anvils or elsewhere on the cutting table, ground to the cutting table.  Serious 
damage to the bearings will result if welding current passes through them. 
 
Following the procedures below will give you optimal durability. However, it will not always be practicable. 
Before welding is started, always 
 check that there is room for both layers. If so, apply both layers and if 
not, apply the wear layer only.  
 
Preheating is always 
 required to ensure long durability. This applies to both top and bottom layers. Before 
starting up the machine check that the shaft turns and that the machine is operational. 
 
TOOLS REQUIRED 
• Propane heater torch and 400-degree heat crayon. 
• Welding equipment with max current = 120-175 Amp 
 
WELDING PROCEDURE 
 
 
 
Entering the hopper/cutting chamber without locking  out the machine could result 
in severe personal injury or death. 
 
1. Lock out the waste reducer (refer the  Locking Out the Waste Reducer section). 
 
2. Enter the hopper/cutting chamber (refer to the Entering the Chamber  section).

3. Before welding is started, clean surface very carefu lly. 
 
 
 
Fire Hazard. 
 
Hydraulic fluids, oils and fuels that are used in the machine can ignite while 
welding. 
 
Clean the area to be welded very carefully to remove flammable fluids. 
 
 
 
Fire Hazard. 
 
Un-processed material in the cutting chamber may ignite while welding 
 
Remove un-processed material prior to welding. 
 
4. When surface is clean, check extent of wear, and check w hich of the following conditions applies: 
 
1. It is the first time a wear layer has been welded  on, or 
2. A wear layer has been welded onto the part at an earlier time. 
 
 
 
Burn Hazard. 
 
Metal surfaces that have been welded are extremely hot. 
 
Do not touch any area of the welded surface until it has cooled. 
 
For condition 1: 
1. Preheat the area to 400 degrees F.  
 
2. Check the size of the worn surface. Build up the wor n area using CN 23/12-FD 309 stainless wire 
with a 95%Ar/5%CO 2 shielding gas mixture. Weld approximately 3/8-inch b eyond the worn area.  
Build up the surface to within 1/8-inch of final dimensions.  
 
NOTE: It is very important that the entire worn area is covered. 
 
3. Weld up to 2 layers on top of the buildup weld as  a wear layer. Use Eutectic/Castolin 6710 XHD, 1/8” 
rod. The number of welds depends on the size and the  shape of the worn area. See illustrations 
below. 
 
NOTE: It is very important that the buildup weld is  covered completely by the wear layer, but 
the wear layer must NOT go beyond the bottom weld. 
 
For condition 2: 
Check whether the wear has spread beyond the area wher e a wear layer has previously been 
welded. If this is the case, first make a buildup wel d on the new surface as described under 
Condition 1. Then weld a wear layer, also described u nder Condition 1. It is not necessary to cut 
or grind off the old weld material.

CUTTER REBUILD EXAMPLE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Make a weld min. 3/8 in beyond the worn area in the d irection shown. Then weld all along the edges and 
the cross must be min. 3/8 in wide. After welding, t he cutter width must not exceed original width. Check 
that the shaft can turn prior to startup. 
 
ANVIL REBUILD EXAMPLE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Make a weld all along the edge. The weld seam must be 3/8 inch wider than the worn area.  
NOTE: Do NOT reduce the original gap between the an vil and cutter! Work inwards, towards the 
center of the anvil, following the arrows. Welding on both sides may be necessary.
